recipes.name: Cheesecake inspired by Junior's Cheesecakes
instructions: For Traditional Cheesecake:
For the Cheesecake Batter

In the bowl of a stand mixer, combine cream cheese, corn starch, sugar, and vanilla extract. Mix on medium speed until completely smooth, 2-3 minutes. - 4 (8 oz) packages cream cheese - ¼ cup corn starch - 333 g sugar - 1 tbsp vanilla extract
Scrape down the sides of the bowl using a rubber spatula, then add the eggs. - 2 large eggs
Add the heavy cream and continue to mix on medium speed until smooth. - ¾ heavy cream
Set aside. - For the Cheesecake Batter
For the Sponge Cake
In a separate bowl of a stand mixer, beat egg yolks on high for 10 minutes, reserving the egg whites. - 2 large egg yolks
Then, slowly stream in granulated sugar and continue beating until the mixture is pale yellow and ribbony, about 2-3 minutes. - 2 tbsp granulated sugar
Continue mixing and add lemon extract and vanilla extract. - 2 tsp lemon extract - 2 tsp vanilla extract
Then, add sifted cake flour and unsalted butter. - ½ cup cake flour sifted - 2 tbsp unsalted butter
Mix until it comes together into a nice yellow batter. Set aside.
In a separate mixing bowl, combine egg whites and cream of tartar. - 2 large egg whites - ½ tsp cream of tartar
Beat with a whisk (by hand or using hand mixer), until frothy, then add granulated sugar and beat until stiff peaks form. - 2 tbsp granulated sugar

Combine ⅓ of the egg whites mixture with the yellow batter, and mix until homogenous. Reintroduce this mixture back into the beaten egg whites, and fold, using a rubber spatula, until smooth. The finished batter should be smooth and pale. - For the Egg Whites Mixture - For the Sponge Cake Batter
Prepare an 8-inch springform pan by lining the outer bottom and sides with a layer of aluminum foil then thoroughly butter the inside. - butter for greasing

Transfer the batter to your prepared springform pan, tap the pan on the counter gently to remove any bubbles, then bake at 350°F for 10 minutes or until the cake has pulled away from the sides of the pan. - For the Sponge Cake Batter
Allow to cool completely. - For the Sponge Cake
Compress the cooled sponge cake using your hands, forming it into a flat, even surface that fills the bottom of the pan. - For the Sponge Cake
For the Cheesecake
Pour the Cheesecake batter on top of the smashed-down Sponge Cake, and tap the springform pan on the counter lightly to remove any bubbles. - For the Cheesecake Batter - For the Sponge Cake
For the Baking
Prepare a water bath by pouring 1 inch of water into the 12-inch cake pan. - 1 inch water
Place your batter-filled, foil-prepared 8-inch springform pan in the 12-inch cake pan water bath and transfer to the oven. - For the Cheesecake Batter

Bake at 300°F for 1 to 2.5 hours depending on oven power. Turn off the oven when about 60% cooked and leave the Cheesecake in the oven until the oven has returned to its normal temperature, about 2 hours. - For the Cheesecake
Remove from the oven and let it rest at room temperature until completely cooled and transfer to the fridge. - For the Cheesecake
Refrigerate for a whole day then remove springform pan sides and serve cold or frozen! - For the Cheesecake
For Strawberry Cheesecake:
For the Cheesecake Batter

In the bowl of a stand mixer, combine cream cheese, corn starch, sugar, and vanilla extract. Mix on medium speed until completely smooth, 2-3 minutes. - 4 (8 oz) packages cream cheese - ¼ cup corn starch - 333 g sugar - 1 tbsp vanilla extract
Scrape down the sides of the bowl using a rubber spatula, then add the eggs. - 2 large eggs
Add the heavy cream and continue to mix on medium speed until smooth. - ¾ heavy cream
Set aside. - For the Cheesecake Batter
For the NIlla Wafer Crust
Add Nilla wafers to a food processor and pulse with baking powder for about 30 seconds until the wafers reduce to fine, even crumbs. - 1 (11 oz) box Nilla Wafers - 1 tsp baking powder
Feed melted butter through the feeding tube and process until the mixture reaches the consistency of wet sand. - 8 tbsp unsalted butter melted
Prepare an 8-inch springform pan by lining the outer bottom and sides with a layer of aluminum foil then thoroughly butter the inside. - butter for greasing

Press Nilla Wafer Curst mixture into the bottom of your prepared springform pan (you can use the bottom of a measuring cup) until the crust is even and flat, reserving some Nilla Wafer Crust mixture for the toppings. - For the Nilla Wafer Crust
Bake at 300°F for about 10 minutes or until the crust is fragrant. - For the Nilla Wafer Crust
Allow to completely. - For the Nilla Wafer Crust
For the Cheesecake

Pour the cheesecake batter atop the completely cooled Nilla Wafer Crust and tap the springform pan on the counter lightly to remove any bubbles. - For the Cheesecake Batter - For the Nilla Wafer Crust
For the Baking
Prepare a water bath by pouring 1 inch of water into the 12-inch cake pan. - 1 inch water
Place your batter-filled, foil-prepared 8-inch springform pan in the 12-inch cake pan water bath and transfer to the oven. - For the Cheesecake Batter

Bake at 300°F for 1 to 2.5 hours depending on oven power. Turn off the oven when about 60% cooked and leave the Cheesecake in the oven until the oven has returned to its normal temperature, about 2 hours. - For the Cheesecake
Remove from the oven and let it rest at room temperature until completely cooled and transfer to the fridge. - For the Cheesecake
Refrigerate for a whole day. - For the Cheesecake
For the Strawberry Topping
While the Cheesecake is cooling, create your Strawberry Topping. - For the Strawberry Topping
Make your strawberry jello according to the package. - 1 pkt strawberry jello
Combine the finished jello with equal parts strawberry jam. Combine until homogeneous. - 1 pkt strawberry jello - strawberry jam
Transfer the mixture to a small saucepan with a 1:1 ratio of cornstarch and water. - 1:1 ratio cornstarch and water - For the Strawberry Topping
Cook and stir until thick and gel-like in consistency. - For the Strawberry Topping
Slice the tops off of the strawberries. - 8 oz strawberries
For the Nilla Wafer Crumble

Add reserved Nilla Wafer Crust mixture to a food processor, then add steel cut oats and process until just crumbled. Add softened butter then pulse to combine. - remaining Nill Wafer Crust mixture - ½ cup steel cut oats - 1 tbsp butter softened
Spread the mixture on a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet and bake at 325°F until brown and crunchy. Allow to cool. - For the Nilla Wafer Crumble
For the Serving

After your Cheesecake has been refrigerated for the whole day, arrange strawberries on top of your chilled Cheesecake and secure with Strawberry Jello mixture. - For the Cheesecake - For the Strawberry Topping - 8 oz strawberries
Then, layer Nilla Wafer Crumbles around the edge of the cake atop the strawberry topping. - For the Cheesecake - For the Strawberry Topping - For the Nilla Wafer Crumble
Remove springform pan sides and serve cold or frozen! - For the Cheesecake
